question: For the CI release profile, compare full-LTO vs thin-LTO vs no-LTO on compile wall, test wall, total, and runtime delta. Only the total decides. Semantic guard: debug-assertions / overflow-checks / panic strategy must be unchanged.
unit_rationale: Exactly the release build validate.sh runs for the release-consuming CI jobs (strict_compat + backend-parity). This is the release compile node whose LTO cost the owner asked about.
semantic_guard: CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO overrides ONLY profile.release.lto. debug-assertions=false, overflow-checks=false, panic=unwind are the release-profile defaults and are NOT touched by this env var, so they are identical across all three rows. LTO is a codegen/link-time optimization and by definition cannot change these determinism-relevant knobs.
current_profile_config: hermit workspace has NO [profile.*] stanzas in any Cargo.toml, no .cargo/config, and no CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO / RUSTFLAGS LTO in any of the 9 CI workflows. Therefore the CI release profile IS cargo's default release profile, whose lto = false. There is no full-LTO in the current CI build.
boxing: systemd-run --user --wait --collect (asks systemd for a scope = still boxed); one clean build per row, run serially
